title: Payments Belong To Their Invoice
description: With several invoices and several retried payments scattered across them, prove the payments-history endpoint — and the foreign key backing it — never lets one invoice's attempts leak into another's list.
successCondition: Create three invoices for three different shipments. Against invoice A, make 2 payment attempts (decline then succeed); against invoice B, make 1 attempt (succeed); leave invoice C with zero attempts. GET /api/billing/invoices/:id/payments for A returns exactly 2 payments, for B exactly 1, for C an empty array. Querying payments via `npm run db:psql` with `select invoice_id, count(*) from payments where invoice_id in ('<A>','<B>','<C>') group by invoice_id` confirms the exact same counts at the database level — no payment row's invoice_id points anywhere other than the invoice it was actually attempted against.
hints: Payment.invoiceId carries a foreign key to Invoice with onDelete Cascade in prisma/schema.prisma — it's a hard relation, not just an application-level convention.
Keep a scratch note of which invoice id is A/B/C as you create them — it's easy to mix them up once you're three shipments deep.
